assets.title: Vascular territories, pons (basilar paramedian vs AICA)
assets.source: Brazis p. 447-448, Vascular Supply of the Pons
notes: Book: paramedian vessels supply the medial basal pons (pontine nuclei, corticospinal fibres, medial lemniscus); AICA supplies the lateral tegmentum of the lower two-thirds of the pons.

Possible inconsistency: the vascular map puts the abducens nucleus and MLF in the basilar paramedian territory, while the Foville card says 'circumferential branches' for a lesion involving the abducens nucleus. Check against the book.

assets.title: Vascular territories, midbrain (peduncular vs thalamoperforating/quadrigeminal)
assets.source: Brazis p. 452, Vascular Supply of the Mesencephalon
notes: POSSIBLE CLINICAL ERROR: the app puts the red nucleus in the 'thalamoperforating & quadrigeminal' territory. The extracted text says the thalamoperforating arteries supply the thalamus, and the peduncular arteries supply the medial peduncles and tegmentum, including the oculomotor nucleus, red nucleus and substantia nigra. Needs your review.
Quadrigeminal arteries supply the superior and inferior colliculi (matches the app).

assets.title: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg)
notes: Atlas card cites pp. 443-446 and the matrix has no page; the first text mention is on p. 441. Verify pages.
Matrix key clue says 'ZERO limb motor weakness'; confirm the wording against the book.

assets.title: Medial medullary (Dejerine)
notes: Atlas card cites pp. 441-443. Extracted text: the ASA supplies the ipsilateral pyramid, medial lemniscus and hypoglossal nerve/nucleus (matches the card).

assets.title: Submedullary (Opalski)
notes: Text matches: lateral medullary syndrome plus ipsilateral hemiplegia from caudal extension below the pyramidal decussation (vertebral artery steno-occlusion or dissection).

assets.title: Millard-Gubler (ventral caudal pons)
notes: App cites pp. 449-450 for the atlas card (the extracted text places it on p. 448; page labels may be off by one).
Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia sparing the face, ipsilateral lateral rectus paresis, ipsilateral peripheral facial paresis.

assets.title: Raymond (ventral medial pons)
notes: App cites p. 450 (extracted text: p. 448).

Content matches (ipsilateral VI, contralateral hemiplegia with central facial paresis). The book adds that later observations challenged the facial involvement and described conjugate gaze palsy from abducens nucleus lesions; the app states facial sparing as fact and omits this.
The book also describes Raymond-Cestan syndrome (p. 448): ipsilateral INO, contralateral cerebellar signs with rubral tremor, contralateral hypesthesia. It is not in the app.

assets.title: Foville (dorsal caudal pontine tegmentum)
notes: App cites p. 450 (extracted text: p. 448).

Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia with facial sparing, ipsilateral peripheral facial palsy, ipsilateral conjugate gaze palsy (PPRF/abducens nucleus). Do not confuse it with the 'midbrain syndrome of Foville' (p. 452).

assets.title: Marie-Foix (lateral pons, brachium pontis)
notes: Matrix only (no atlas card).
Text: ipsilateral cerebellar ataxia, contralateral hemiparesis, variable contralateral pain/temperature hemihypesthesia (matches).
NOT in the book text: 'occasional CN VII / VIII' and the vessel 'AICA / lateral pontine branches' shown in the matrix.

assets.title: Locked-in syndrome (bilateral basis pontis)
notes: Matrix only (no atlas card).
Text says 'occasional impairment of horizontal eye movements' (bilateral VI fascicles); the matrix states 'bilateral horizontal gaze palsy' without the qualifier.
Matrix text uses 'SRAA' (a Spanish acronym) where the English UI should say ARAS (ascending reticular activating system).

assets.title: Weber (ventral midbrain, crus cerebri)
notes: App cites pp. 452-453.
Content matches: contralateral hemiplegia including lower facial weakness, ipsilateral oculomotor paresis with dilated pupil.

assets.title: Benedikt (midbrain tegmentum, red nucleus)
notes: App cites pp. 453-454.
Text: ipsilateral oculomotor paresis, contralateral hemiataxia with intention tremor (red nucleus), contralateral hemiparesis with hyperactive reflexes; usually PCA branch infarction.

NOT in the book text: 'chorea / choreoathetosis' and 'variable medial lemniscus impairment' (the atlas card, matrix and flowchart say chorea). The text lists intention tremor / hemiataxia from the red nucleus and mentions hemiballismus only to say Claude syndrome has none. Needs your decision: keep as an external fact or remove.
The app's vessel 'thalamoperforating' conflicts with the book's peduncular arteries (see vascular/midbrain).

assets.title: Claude (dorsal midbrain tegmentum)
notes: App cites p. 454 (extracted text: p. 453).

Text: 'similar clinical manifestations' to Benedikt, from a more dorsal tegmental lesion injuring the dorsal red nucleus and brachium conjunctivum, with prominent cerebellar signs (asynergia, ataxia, dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia) and no hemiballismus.

POSSIBLE OVERSTATEMENT: the app says 'pure cerebellar hemiataxia' and 'NO tremor or chorea'. The book says the picture is similar to Benedikt (which includes intention tremor) and only excludes hemiballismus. Needs your review.

assets.title: Parinaud (dorsal midbrain / Sylvian aqueduct)
notes: App cites pp. 454-456 (extracted text: p. 453).
Content matches: upward gaze paralysis (occasionally down-gaze), large pupils with light-near dissociation, convergence-retraction nystagmus, Collier sign.
